task: Each time a client arrives, take their order, get food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and hand it over; should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), hard Response(client_arrived, food_prepared), hard Response(client_arrived, order_served), hard Response(client_arrived, order_taken)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task states a sequence inside the 'each time a client arrives' wording — 'take their order, get food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and hand it over'. Per the 'whenever a: do b, then c, then d' pattern, each step must follow the one before it, never all from client_arrived. The candidate instead uses Response(client_arrived, food_prepared) and Response(client_arrived, order_served), which drop the stated order between the steps as clauses (a serve tied only to the arrival, not to the prepare step that precedes it). Replace them with Response(order_taken, food_prepared) and Response(food_prepared, order_served), both hard. Keep Response(client_arrived, order_taken) and the hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), which correctly captures 'should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up'; the pantry fetch (a lasting holding_food condition) rightly gets no clause.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), hard Response(client_arrived, order_taken), hard Response(food_prepared, order_served), hard Response(order_taken, food_prepared)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: The task is a 'whenever a: b, then c, then d' chain with a slip-recovery rule. Response(client_arrived, order_taken), Response(order_taken, food_prepared), and Response(food_prepared, order_served) correctly express 'each time a client arrives, take their order, ... prepare it ... and hand it over' (the pantry fetch is a lasting condition step, holding_food, and rightly gets no clause of its own). ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food) captures 'should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up', and it is satisfiable since a slip turns the agent to face the food and no new slip is planned until a new pickup. All clauses are hard as the wording demands, all propositions are declared, and the rule-only warning is valid: every requirement is scoped by 'each time' or 'should', so no unconditional goal exists and an empty FINAL_STATES is correct.
